headline: All majors below the 200-day line, momentum diverging, and whales rotating out of spot while longs remain crowded on leverage.
paragraphs: The market structure is uniformly bearish. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and not one has a golden cross in formation. This is not a mixed regime; it is a regime. Bitcoin sits at 63,923, down 48.8 percent from its 12-month high of 124,740, and Ethereum is worse at 60.5 percent below peak. Solana and Doge are both off by over 70 percent from their annual highs. The entire leadership cohort is pressed into the bear structure simultaneously.

Momentum is now decoupling from the downtrend in a way that deserves attention. Bitcoin's RSI-14 is neutral at 48.7, and its MACD remains below the signal line, which confirms the weakness; but Ethereum, despite being down 60 percent on the year, still carries an RSI of 55.8. More strikingly, BNB and Doge both show MACD above the signal line even as price remains well below the 200-day average. This is classic divergence: the selling impulse has not accelerated, and on certain names a subtle momentum lift is already appearing within the downtrend. That does not reverse the downtrend. It flags that the pace of weakness may be slowing.

Leverage positioning shows longs are still the crowded bet. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio sits at 1.41, Ethereum at 1.54, and Solana at 2.74. These are not extreme ratios, but they are long-heavy. Funding on Bitcoin annualizes at 10.4 percent, meaning longs are still paying to hold the trade; on Ethereum, funding is tamer at 2.6 percent annually. The 24-hour liquidation data shows 1,228 closures on Bitcoin with long liquidations of 7.1 million against short liquidations of 4.2 million. Ethereum saw 1,600 liquidations with a roughly 56-44 split toward long closeouts. Money is exiting longs, but the long bias persists.

Whale behavior, however, tells a different story. Over the past 72 hours, the net flow is off exchanges by 147.4 million dollars, and Bitcoin is the center of it. Whales withdrew 226 million dollars net from spot markets, with 146.3 million leaving Coinbase Institutional alone and 115.3 million from Kraken. Simultaneously, 139.7 million went onto Coinbase Institutional and 119 million to OKX. This is churn and rotation, not a clean unidirectional move. The weekly net for the past month shows oscillation: 996 million out, then 148 million in, then 138 million in, then 739 million out again. Whales are churning position, not establishing a clear bid. Stablecoin float sits at 304.5 billion, down 1.6 percent over 30 days, which signals the dry powder is not replenishing significantly.

The Fear and Greed index reads 28, labeled Fear, near the lower end of its 30-day range of 11 to 33. Sentiment is fearful but not panicked; the crowd is not in crisis mode. Yet the spot ETF picture on Bitcoin shows 32.1 million in on July 29, the latest day, offsetting what was a five-session net of negative 494.4 million. Traditional finance participation has drained. Ethereum's ETF saw negative 32.9 million on the same day, with the five-session net at negative 56.2 million. The TradFi bid is absent. Total market cap fell 0.49 percent on the day to 2.27 trillion, and Bitcoin dominance stands at 56.5 percent, a position of strength relative to the altcoins.

Watch for two conditions: a reclaim by Bitcoin above the 200-day simple moving average would reset the structural regime and force momentum followers to reassess; and a flip in whale net direction from off-exchange back to on-exchange over a five-day window would signal renewal of accumulation pressure. Until then, the picture is a downtrend with diverging momentum and leverage that is still long-biased but shedding longs under price. Funding remains positive on Bitcoin, which means the longs paying to hold are still willing to pay, but at lower cost than weeks prior. The regime has not turned; it has begun to pause.
